---
title: "What are OSPOs trying to achieve?"
---

# Overview

Title says it all, really.

Research questions:
- Who does your OSPO primarily serve?\
- What are the main objectives of your OSPO or OSPO-like function?\
- Does your OSPO currently track any metrics or indicators of its impact?\
- What is your elevator pitch for why your OSPO matters?\
- Which audiences do you engage with regularly as part of your Open Source work?


# Import packages, utilities, and config variables
```{r}
library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(docstring)
library(readr)
library(tibble)

source("utils.R")

# Read config.yml
cfg <- config::get()
```


# Load data
```{r}
mc_simple <- read_tsv(file.path(cfg$data_path, "mc_simple.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE, skip_empty_rows = FALSE)
org_responses <- read_excel(file.path(cfg$curated_path, "orgs.xlsx"), sheet="responses")
ospo_loc <- read_tsv(file.path(cfg$data_path, "ospo_location.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE, skip_empty_rows = FALSE)
objs <- read_tsv(file.path(cfg$data_path, "objectives.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE, skip_empty_rows = FALSE)
matrix_other <- read_tsv(file.path(cfg$data_path, "matrix_other.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE, skip_empty_rows = FALSE)
qual <- read_tsv(file.path(cfg$data_path, "qual.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE, skip_empty_rows = FALSE)
auds <- read_tsv(file.path(cfg$data_path, "audiences.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE, skip_empty_rows = FALSE)
codebook <- read_excel(file.path(cfg$data_path, "codebook.xlsx"))
```

# Scope
What is each OSPO's scope? Hopefully responses from the same institution match, but let's check. 
```{r}
org_responses$scope <- mc_simple$scope
dupes <- org_responses |>
  group_by(organization) |>
  filter(n() > 1) |> 
  ungroup()

# Keep commented for privacy!!
# dupes |> select(-response)
```

Okay, well, there is one disagreement, but I know that university, and they're not part of an OSPO Network, so I'm pretty inclined to side with respondent 1 over respondent 2 on this and say they serve their own institution, and no other institutions. I think the intent of the "beyond our institution" thing was really about official services like OSPO networks. And the question says who do you "primarily" serve.

Since the person I agree with happens to occur first, I can just do what I did in the last notebook: grab the first occurrence of the institution. I think I will leave in the one Network-level response this time, because I think it's relevant here.

```{r}
# We don't need this column
org_responses <- org_responses |> select(-response)

# Get a summary table of items and their first row index
tmp <- org_responses |>
  mutate(row_idx = row_number()) |>
  group_by(organization) |>
  summarise(first_occurrence_idx = min(row_idx), .groups = "drop")

rows_to_keep <- sort(tmp$first_occurrence_idx)

# One response per org
org_responses_filt <- org_responses[rows_to_keep, ]
nrow(org_responses_filt)
```

```{r}
table(org_responses_filt$scope)
```

# Objectives

This was a matrix question. I'll start by recoding the likert scale responses to numbers.

```{r}
score_map <- c(
  "Not an objective for us"  = 0L,
  "A minor consideration"   = 1L,
  "Important, but secondary" = 2L,
  "A core objective"        = 3L
)

# Convert all text columns to numeric values
objs_numeric <- objs |>
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ score_map[.x]))
```

## Per-OSPO

I strongly suspect that there will be differences between responses from the same institution. Let's check.

```{r}
org_objs <- cbind(org_responses$organization, objs_numeric)
names(org_objs)[1] <- "organization"
dupes2 <- org_objs |>
  group_by(organization) |>
  filter(n() > 1) |>
  arrange(organization, .by_group = TRUE)

# Keep commented for privacy!!
# dupes2
```

As expected, responses from the same institution do not match perfectly. However, they are pretty similar (which is good!). I'm going to take an average from the orgs that had multiple responses, and I'll use that to calculate the institution's score. 

```{r}
# Uh-oh, I'm getting NAs. Which rows have NAs?
which(is.na(objs_numeric), arr.ind = TRUE)
```

I see one person gave all NA responses to this question. I will remove them.

```{r}
# N.B. this removes rows with NA in ANY column
dim(org_objs)
org_objs <- na.omit(org_objs)
dim(org_objs)
```

I'm just going to take the average score per organization.

```{r}
org_objs_avgd <- org_objs |>
  group_by(organization) |>
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)))

dim(org_objs_avgd)
# Keep commented for privacy!!
# org_objs_avgd
```

Check out the overall scores for each objective
```{r}
sort(colSums(org_objs_avgd[,-1]), decreasing = TRUE)
```

### Objectives by OSPO location
Feedback from Clare: does the objective vary based on OSPO location?

First, we'll get one set of locations for each OSPO using my heuristic: if anyone from that organization said yes, then that organization's response is yes.

```{r}
ospo_loc$organization <- org_responses$organization
ospo_loc_filtered <- consolidate_org_responses_yn(ospo_loc)
dim(ospo_loc_filtered)
```

For interpretable results, let's look at TTO-only OSPOs and library-only OSPOs.

```{r}
# Merge the (filtered) location and objective dataframes 
loc_obj <- left_join(ospo_loc_filtered, org_objs_avgd, by = "organization")
# Remove the "joint" column which is unnecessary and confusing
loc_obj <- subset(loc_obj, select = -joint)
dim(loc_obj)
```

```{r}
lib_only <- loc_obj |>
  filter(
    library == "Yes",
    if_all(admin:ai_institute, ~ .x == "No")
  )

lib_scores <- lib_only |>
  select(where(is.numeric)) |>
  colSums(na.rm = TRUE)

sort(lib_scores, decreasing = TRUE)
```

```{r}
tto_only <- loc_obj |>
  filter(
    tto == "Yes",
    if_all(
      where(~ all(.x %in% c("Yes", "No"), na.rm = TRUE)) & !tto,
      ~ .x == "No"
    )
  )

tto_scores <- tto_only |>
  select(where(is.numeric)) |>
  colSums(na.rm = TRUE)

sort(tto_scores, decreasing = TRUE)
```

Cool. We can see at a glance that there are some differences here, especially in policy and community.

```{r}
# Spearman's rho test (uses t-approximation due to ties in tto_scores)
spearman_res <- cor.test(tto_scores, lib_scores, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)
print(spearman_res)
```

Looks like the rank orders are significantly different.

### Other locations
```{r}
admin_only <- loc_obj |>
  filter(
    admin == "Yes",
    if_all(
      where(~ all(.x %in% c("Yes", "No"), na.rm = TRUE)) & !admin,
      ~ .x == "No"
    )
  )

admin_scores <- admin_only |>
  select(where(is.numeric)) |>
  colSums(na.rm = TRUE)

sort(admin_scores, decreasing = TRUE)
```

## Per-person

Does taking everybody's response equally, without any average, affect the ranking?

```{r}
# N.B. this removes rows with NA in ANY column
dim(objs_numeric)
objs_numeric <- na.omit(objs_numeric)
dim(objs_numeric)

sort(colSums(objs_numeric), decreasing = TRUE)
```

Policy, support, and engagement are switched around, but everything else is the same as before. 

The person who answered NA to objectives did answer the question about location. Let's keep them in, join the data frames, and then remove them.

```{r}
# Convert all text columns to numeric values
objs_numeric_keep_NA <- objs |>
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ score_map[.x]))
org_objs2 <- cbind(org_responses$organization, objs_numeric_keep_NA)
names(org_objs2)[1] <- "organization"

# Make sure the rows correspond
identical(org_objs2$organization, ospo_loc$organization)

# Join data frames
loc_obj_per_person <- cbind(org_objs_keep_NA, ospo_loc)
# Remove all rows that contain any NA 
loc_obj_per_person <- na.omit(loc_obj_per_person)
# Drop unneeded columns
loc_obj_per_person <- loc_obj_per_person |> select(-organization, -joint)
head(loc_obj_per_person)
```

Now let's do what we did before, splitting into library vs. TTO groups, but this time our sample size will be a bit larger because we are counting respondents, not organizations.

```{r}
lib_only_pp <- loc_obj_per_person |>
  filter(
    library == "Yes",
    if_all(admin:ai_institute, ~ .x == "No")
  )

lib_scores_pp <- lib_only_pp |>
  select(where(is.numeric)) |>
  colSums(na.rm = TRUE)

sort(lib_scores_pp, decreasing = TRUE)
```

```{r}
tto_only_pp <- loc_obj_per_person |>
  filter(
    tto == "Yes",
    if_all(
      where(~ all(.x %in% c("Yes", "No"), na.rm = TRUE)) & !tto,
      ~ .x == "No"
    )
  )

tto_scores_pp <- tto_only_pp |>
  select(where(is.numeric)) |>
  colSums(na.rm = TRUE)

sort(tto_scores_pp, decreasing = TRUE)
```
```{r}
# Spearman's rho test (uses t-approximation due to ties in tto_scores)
spearman_res <- cor.test(tto_scores_pp, lib_scores_pp, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)
print(spearman_res)
```
Again the ranks are not correlated.


# Metrics
This was a slightly sneaky "simple multiple choice" question in that it doesn't use an "other" field, but it was followed by a very closely related qualitative question. Let's save those qualitative answers to a file for coding. Note that for this one we are NOT filtering to one response per institution.

```{r}
write_df_to_file(qual$metrics_other, "metrics.txt", path_key = "coding_path")
```

As before, let's inspect the responses from the same university and see if they are in accord with one another.

```{r}
org_metrics <- org_responses
org_metrics$metrics <- mc_simple$metrics
# We don't need this column
org_metrics <- org_metrics |> select(-scope)
dupes <- org_metrics |>
  group_by(organization) |>
  filter(n() > 1) |> 
  arrange(metrics, .by_group = TRUE)

# Keep commented for privacy!!
# dupes
```

Bah! They mostly agree, but there is one institution where the respondents disagree (2 responses total). I'm just going to pick one at random. I'll just pick whichever response comes first.

```{r}
# One response per org
org_metrics_filt <- org_metrics[rows_to_keep, ]
```

```{r}
table(org_metrics_filt$metrics)
```
